header: Function    : Print the transaction detail report.
purpose.rationale: prints the transaction detail report for a date range

errorHandling.behaviour: Any unexpected file status displays a message and the file status (as 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' + 4 digits), then abends with code 999 (CALL 'CEE3ABD'). The step return code becomes 16 and later steps do not run.

files.volatileFieldsBasis: flow-insensitive byte-range taint from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE / WHEN-COMPILED and ACCEPT FROM DATE|TIME|DAY, propagated through MOVE (byte-mapped for alphanumeric and group moves), arithmetic, STRING, UNSTRING and WRITE/REWRITE FROM

legacyQuirks.description: NEXT SENTENCE transfers control past the next period, not to the end of the enclosing IF; inside an inline PERFORM it leaves the loop.

After end of file the ELSE of 'IF END-OF-FILE = 'N'' uses TRAN-AMT from the record area, which still holds the last record read (DISPLAY 'TRAN-AMT ' TRAN-AMT; DISPLAY 'WS-PAGE-TOTAL' WS-PAGE-TOTAL; ADD TRAN-AMT TO WS-PAGE-TOTAL WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL; PERFORM 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS; PERFORM 1110-WRITE-GRAND-TOTALS).
On INVALID KEY the INTO record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) keeps the previously read record's values.
On INVALID KEY the INTO record (TRAN-TYPE-RECORD) keeps the previously read record's values.
On INVALID KEY the INTO record (TRAN-CAT-RECORD) keeps the previously read record's values.

semantics: Numeric receivers keep their PICTURE: integer digits beyond the PICTURE are truncated on the left (no ON SIZE ERROR is coded), fraction digits beyond the scale are truncated (no ROUNDED unless stated), an unsigned receiver stores the absolute value.
COMPUTE evaluates exactly, then stores with the receiver's truncation; division results are truncated at the receiver's scale.
Zoned decimal files carry the sign as an EBCDIC-style overpunch in the last byte ({ A-I positive, } J-R negative); unsigned fields hold plain digits.
Storage without a VALUE clause starts as binary zeros (x'00'); STRING does not pad its receiver.
DISPLAY of an unsigned numeric field prints its digits with leading zeros; DISPLAY of a group prints its raw bytes.
Alphanumeric receivers are left-justified and space-padded; comparisons of alphanumerics are byte-wise after space padding.
INDEXED files are fixed-length record images kept in primary-key order; SEQUENTIAL files are fixed-length records.
FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE gives YYYYMMDDHHMMSShh+hhmm from the batch clock; the DB2 timestamp built from it is YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000.

acceptance.oracle: GnuCOBOL 3.3 running the original source (-std=ibm -fsign=EBCDIC), storage default x'00'
acceptance.equality: Every output dataset byte-identical; SYSOUT line-identical; same return code. Fields listed as volatile may differ only when the clock is not pinned.
acceptance.clock: Tests pin the batch clock (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE) to a fixed instant.

designContract.output: One JSON document conforming to design.schema.json (mlcpu.capability-design.v1).
rules: Express business rules as typed Java over immutable records (BigDecimal for amounts, enums for reason codes, Optional for lookups).
Keep file formats behind repository/port interfaces; business services must not see byte offsets, file status codes or record images.
Every rule id in 'rules' must be traced to a design element, or dispositioned as 'not-needed' with a reason.
Every legacy quirk must be dispositioned: 'preserve' (needed for output parity) or 'fix' (behaviour change, requires business sign-off).
Every console line and output dataset in observableOutputs must be produced by a named design element.
Do not invent behaviour that the packet does not evidence.
